thread_title: S. flava 'all red' (L x best clone) Liberty Co, FL
breadcrumb: S. flava 'all red' (L x best clone) Liberty Co, FL

posts.body_html:
Solid red flavas have multiple different pathways of origin, but one pathway that I've been exploring for the past decade or so is by crossing 2 different rubricorpora clones with each other. In the past, I've made perhaps more than 10 different rubricorpora x rubricorpora crosses, and so far only 2 have yielded solid red plants. For more information on the first cross, check out this post: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/273/flava-var-atropurpurea-liberty-fl

here's a different clone of a solid red flava using the same concept: 2 different rubricorporas were crossed together. In this case, the parents to this all red plant are S. flava var. rubricorpora (L x best clone). What's also notable is how the interior of the trap is greenish, but I can't remember if this fades away or not as the trap ages. From this cross, I literally grew out over 200 plants, and 2 of them turned out solid red. This suggests getting red plants from such a cross requires growing out a large number of individuals.


The traps just opened, so they haven't fully colored up yet, photos taken 4/24/17. This clone is vigorous and performs well year after year:









I'll try to get more pics up as this trap ages, hopefully it doesn't get fried like it did last year.....

posts.body_html: I think I missed this post until now - thanks for digging it up Heath! Gorgeous plant. Did you bag the flowers when you made that cross meizzwang? If not, I’d bet money that your Liberty county got partially OP’d with a flava cuprea. The shape and veining, plus the noticeably bronze cast to the lid look very much like the rubri x cupreas I’ve seen. That said, I’ve seen plants in Liberty Co. that did have some burnt sugar shades in the lids, at least with age.
